narrative.overview:
The site is a white room with black type and one lime signal. Everything structural is monochrome: ink-black headlines, white space, pale grey panels. One color, Signal Lime, marks where to look or what to do: the drifting hero circle, the active language, an open accordion row, the primary call to action, the chat launcher. The visitor is usually a skeptical buyer checking whether Web41 is real, and the restraint does the persuading: big bold type, short copy and real project imagery, with nothing decorative between them and the next step.

The mood is confident, airy and direct. Density is low. Headlines run large (60–88px display, 36–60px section heads), body copy sits at 18px at 80% opacity, and sections breathe with 80px gutters on desktop. Motion is slow and physical, never flashy: the lime circle rises in and drifts with scroll on a soft spring, project covers zoom 5% on hover, accordions open on a 300ms grid-row transition, and every effect yields to `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Components are confident and tactile: 56px pill buttons in bold type that lift 2px on hover and press to 98% on click; flat grey cards with 8px corners; full-width accordion rows (Services and FAQ) split by hairline dividers. The site is also the sales proof, so the system has to hold up next to whatever it sells.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome structure (black, white, two greys) with a single lime accent.
One typeface, Fixel Display, in four weights; hierarchy comes from size and weight, not from mixing families.
Pills and circles for anything interactive or signalling; 8px corners for content containers.
Flat surfaces; depth comes from tone (#f9f9f9 panels on white) and only floating UI gets a shadow.
Slow, springy, scroll-linked motion that always has a reduced-motion fallback.
Muted-grey words inside black headlines carry the rhythm of the display line.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Lime is the only hue on the page and covers well under 10% of any viewport. It marks attention, state or the next action. Never use it as a section background, a text color or decoration.

rules.name: The Opacity, Not Greys Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is Ink Black at reduced opacity (80 / 70 / 60%), not new grey hexes. Slate Mute exists only for the muted headline words.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Fixel Display is the only typeface, in four weights only. Build hierarchy with size and weight; do not add a second family or a fifth weight.

rules.name: The Muted Word Rule
rules.body: Display headlines may fade one or more phrases to Slate Mute to set the rhythm of the line. The key promise stays Ink Black.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards, sections and inputs never carry a shadow at rest. A shadow is either a response to the pointer or the mark of a floating layer.

rules.name: The Round-Means-Action Rule
rules.body: Pills and circles are reserved for interactive or signalling elements. Content blocks use 8px corners; never round a card into a pill.

dos: Do keep Signal Lime (#dbff04) for state and attention: active, open, hovered row, primary signal, the hero circle. One lime moment per viewport is the norm.
Do set lime surfaces with Ink Black text and icons only.
Do build secondary text from Ink Black at 80 / 70 / 60% opacity.
Do use Fixel Display for everything, at 400, 500, 600 or 700.
Do make every interactive control at least 44px tall (buttons 44 or 56px, nav links 44px min height).
Do give every motion a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback, as the circle, marquees and buttons already have.
Do keep the 2px black focus outline at 2px offset (white on the footer); inside clipped rows, inset it with a negative offset.
Do keep cards flat Mist Grey with 8px corners, and reserve shadows for hover lift and floating chat or menu layers.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue or tint lime into gradients or backgrounds.
Don't use Signal Lime as a text color or a full-section background.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, sections or inputs at rest.
Don't add a second typeface or extra weights of Fixel Display.
Don't round content containers into pills, or square off buttons; round means action.
Don't introduce new grey hex values for text when an Ink Black opacity step will do.
Don't fill empty metric chips, testimonial slots or logo rows with placeholder data; leave the element out.
